updated: Commands as registered by the bot

commands.name: ping
commands.panel: A reply with Check again, Start setup and Health check buttons
commands.summary: Live health, measured the moment you run it: gateway heartbeat, uptime, Node version, memory, the server it is in, commands registered, saved servers with their addresses, how many staff role slots are filled (and any that point at a role that no longer exists), how many log types are set (and any channel the bot cannot post in), whether the setup gate is passed, and a real request to this website with the round-trip time.
commands.why: Nothing. It works before setup is finished, and it says which step is still missing.

commands.name: help
commands.panel: Buttons that open each command's own page, plus the command option
commands.summary: What every command does, who may run it and what each one needs set up first. Name a command to jump straight to its page.
commands.why: Nothing. It only reports and links.

subcommands.name: command
subcommands.summary: Name a command to open its own help page straight away. Run it bare for the home panel: one button per command, a Start setup button while setup is unfinished, and the website links.
notes: The setup note on the home panel is read from what is saved, so it cannot be out of date.

commands.name: setup
commands.who: Administrator, Manage Server or the server owner
commands.panel: Click-to-pick panels: role lists, channel lists, health checks and pasteable server lines
commands.summary: Configure Spinback for your server without copying a single id. Staff roles come from a list, log channels from a list or made for you, and the Rust connection is tested before anything is saved — so a wrong port or password never lands in your settings.
commands.why: The RCON port and password from server.cfg, with rcon.web set to 0.

subcommands.name: run
subcommands.summary: The main panel: roles, log channels, the Rust server, plus Find them for me, Health check, Import, Export and Reset.
notes: Every step is a picker or a button. Nothing is inferred from a name unless the panel says it was.

subcommands.name: roles
subcommands.summary: Pick each staff role straight from this server's role list, one slot at a time. Choose nothing in the list to clear a slot.
notes: The roles saved here are the staff roles: they, Administrator, Manage Server and the server owner may run every staff command.

subcommands.name: channels
subcommands.summary: Logging channels two ways: pick a log type then its channel, or have the bot create a Spinback category and one channel per type you tick.
notes: A type with no channel is simply switched off. Creating channels is the only step that makes anything in your server, and it shows the exact list first.

subcommands.name: server
subcommands.summary: Add or change the Rust server, either by typing the details or by pasting the RCON lines from server.cfg.

subcommands.name: suggest
subcommands.summary: Read the role and channel names in this server and propose a match for each slot and log type, with the matching reason shown for every line, then apply the whole list in one press.
notes: A name match is a suggestion, never a decision: Apply writes exactly the list that was on screen.

subcommands.name: doctor
subcommands.summary: The health check: saved role ids are checked against this server, every log channel is checked for reachability, each saved Rust server is asked a real RCON command and timed, the kit commands are checked for their {player} and {kit} placeholders, storage is checked, and then it lists what to fix first.
notes: It opens up to three fresh RCON connections and changes nothing.

subcommands.name: import
subcommands.summary: Paste the RCON lines from server.cfg (or host port password on one line). The bot reads them, says which pieces it found and which are missing, warns when rcon.web is 1, then tests the connection and only saves if the server answers.
notes: Nothing is filled in: a field it did not find is reported as missing.

subcommands.name: export
subcommands.summary: Everything saved, as text you can copy: role slots with role names, log channels with channel names, the kit commands, the servers and the player link counts.
notes: No RCON password is in the export at all — it never leaves the service that talks to your server.

subcommands.name: reset
subcommands.summary: Clear the saved configuration again after typing RESET in capitals.
notes: Player links, waiting requests and the link panel message are kept. No channel, role or player is deleted.

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.summary: A checklist of what is saved and what is still missing, with counts for roles, channels, servers, kit binds and respawn kits.

subcommands.name: edit
subcommands.summary: Change a saved server's address, RCON port or password. New details are tested before anything is saved.

subcommands.name: refresh
subcommands.summary: Open a fresh RCON connection and report exactly what the server answers, in its own words.

options.name: server
options.description: Server name to test. Leave it blank to test the first saved one.

commands.name: kits
commands.who: Staff roles, Administrator, Manage Server or the owner
commands.summary: Emote kits end to end: the real kit names from your server, binds with cooldowns and roles, handing kits out, clearing cooldowns, respawn kits per auth group, and installing kits built in Kit Studio.
commands.why: Your kit plugin's own command names, and a give template using {player} and {kit}. The bot will not guess either one.

subcommands.name: commands
subcommands.summary: Set your kit plugin's own list command, give template and install command — the settings nothing else could set from Discord.
notes: The give template is filled with {player} and {kit}; the install command with {code}. Leave a field blank when saving to clear that command.

subcommands.name: doctor
subcommands.summary: Check the kit setup: which commands are set, whether the give template really has both placeholders, every bind, the respawn kits for each group, the lock state and the install codes held.
notes: Read-only, and it sends nothing to your server: a kit name is only ever checked against what the plugin itself reports.

subcommands.name: grab
subcommands.summary: Read the real kit names from your Rust server instead of taking a typed list.
notes: Needs your list command set first: the bot will not invent the name of one.

subcommands.name: config
subcommands.summary: The emote kit wizard: binds, cooldowns, roles, lock kits and the emote guide.

subcommands.name: give
subcommands.summary: Hand a kit to a gamertag or to a linked Discord user.

options.name: kit
options.description: Kit name. Leave it blank to open the panel instead.

options.name: gamertag
options.description: In-game name to give it to.

options.name: user
options.description: Discord user whose linked gamertag receives it.

notes: Blank options open the panel rather than guessing a target.

subcommands.name: refresh
subcommands.summary: Clear kit cooldowns for one user, one kit, everyone, or every kit.

options.name: scope
options.description: What to clear. Leave blank to open the panel.

options.name: target
options.description: Gamertag or kit name, when the scope needs one.

subcommands.name: auth-spawn
subcommands.summary: Give a kit to an auth group on every respawn.

options.name: group
options.description: Auth group. Leave blank to open the panel.

options.name: kit
options.description: Kit to hand out. Blank stops giving one.

subcommands.name: cooldowns
subcommands.summary: See the kit cooldown records the bot is holding right now.

subcommands.name: build
subcommands.summary: Open Kit Studio on this website, or work from an install code.

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.summary: Install a kit from a Base64 kit install code.

options.name: code
options.description: The Base64 install code. Leave blank to open the panel.

commands.name: user
commands.who: Staff roles, Administrator, Manage Server or the owner
commands.panel: Pickers and modals, plus a member-facing link panel
commands.summary: Player links: the bot's record of which Discord account belongs to which gamertag. Everything player-facing in Spinback runs on this list.
commands.why: One staff role and one tested Rust server, because links feed the panels that use them.

subcommands.name: whois
subcommands.summary: Look up which Discord account is behind a gamertag, or part of one. It prints ids as text, so looking somebody up cannot notify or ping them.
notes: Requests that are still waiting are shown too, labelled as waiting rather than linked.

subcommands.name: pending
subcommands.summary: Every request waiting for confirmation, with an Approve and a Reject button per person. Approving writes the link as you, so the record shows who confirmed it.
notes: A request is a claim, not proof — this is where a person turns it into a link, or throws it out.

subcommands.name: forcelink
subcommands.summary: Link a Discord user to a gamertag yourself. This is how a genuine request gets approved.

subcommands.name: forceunlink
subcommands.summary: Remove a player link, after a confirmation panel.

subcommands.name: transfer
subcommands.summary: Move a link to a new Discord account or a new gamertag.

subcommands.name: linkpanel
subcommands.summary: Post a member-facing panel with Link account and Unlink buttons in a channel.

options.name: channel
options.description: Channel to post it in. Leave blank to pick from a list.

notes: Members press the buttons themselves; the bot checks who is asking before it changes a link.

subcommands.name: roster
subcommands.summary: Everyone who is linked, with their gamertag and Discord account.

commands.name: server
commands.who: Staff roles, Administrator, Manage Server or the owner
commands.panel: A reply with Ask again and a jump to setup
commands.summary: Ask your Rust server over RCON without changing anything. Only the commands on the bot's fixed allowed list are ever sent: serverinfo, playerlist, gettime and status. Whatever the server answers is shown exactly as it arrived, with the round-trip time.
commands.why: Setup finished — one staff role and one tested Rust server, because a connection is what answers these.

subcommands.name: info
subcommands.summary: Name, players online, map and uptime, as the server reports them.

subcommands.name: players
subcommands.summary: The names and ping the server reports for everyone online.

subcommands.name: time
subcommands.summary: The in-game clock.

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.summary: The server's own status answer, exactly as it arrives.

subcommands.name: check
subcommands.summary: Open a fresh RCON connection right now and time it.
notes: Useful after a fix: it is the same test that decides whether a server can be saved.
